headline: Computational tools refine cell segmentation and spatial molecular state inference
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Methods
summary: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics methods now demand computational tools for foci detection, cell segmentation and clustering stability.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational extraction of cell-level and molecular information from imaging-based and spatial transcriptomic data. PhySeqNet trains annotation-free U-Net detectors on physics-based semi-synthetic BARseq images to improve fluorescent foci detection, while CellART combines staining images with scRNA-seq references to segment cells. STARIT encodes transcripts within segmented cells as rasterized image tensors for deep vision models, a representation distinct from graph-based approaches. InSTability scores per-spot clustering instability across random seeds with linear-time scaling. Point-process modelling of CosMx glioma data links cell-type interactions to molecular states, though cross-patient transfer is limited. Several items, including FilAdh, SatelliteQ and the c-TSNE work, address related imaging or scRNA-seq analysis rather than spatial inference.
